name: JMSFusion
description: Frontend enhancement plugin for Jellyfin Web and web-wrapper mobile clients; native Android TV clients are not supported.
overview: Custom script loader for the Jellyfin web UI.

versions.changelog:
v3.7.1.1 (custom fork)

Follow-up to 3.7.1.0. The details panel now previews the episode you point at,
shows you which ones you have already seen, and the settings ship the way this
server should behave instead of having to be set by hand.

Hover an episode:
- It played the series trailer from YouTube — the same clip for every episode of
  the show. It now plays the episode itself, streamed from your server.
- The video at the top of the panel pauses while you are previewing, so two
  soundtracks no longer play at once, and resumes where it was when you move
  away.

See what you have already watched:
- Watched episodes get a check mark and their thumbnail dims.
- Half-watched ones get a progress bar showing how far you got.

Smaller changes to the panel:
- The TMDb Reviews section at the bottom is gone, along with the request it made
  every time the panel opened.
- "Add to my list" now reads "Add to favorites". The button always toggled
  Jellyfin favourites; only the wording was wrong.
- Report a problem has a sixth choice, "Other", for anything the five fixed
  options do not cover.

Settings now ship configured:
- Trailers start at 40% volume instead of full.
- Slider hover plays trailer, then video.
- Hover type is StudioHubs Mini, with the trailer popover on.
- Original title is hidden when it matches the title; director and writer info
  is off.
- Notifications: toasts for system messages only, not for newly added content,
  and system messages stay out of the unread counter. Unfinished watching is
  shown.
- These are applied once on upgrade, to existing profiles as well as new ones.
  Anything you change afterwards is kept.

Fixes:
- Saving settings while hover type was StudioHubs Mini silently turned off
  "Trailer > Play Video", because the browser omits disabled checkboxes when
  submitting a form.

Notes:
- Restart Jellyfin after install
- Hard refresh (Ctrl + F5) once after upgrading

v3.7.1.0 (custom fork)

The details page — the panel that opens when you click a poster — reworked
around playing something rather than reading about it.

Fills the screen:
- It opened as a fixed 1000x900 card. It now uses the whole window.
- Width alone would not have helped the episode list: episode descriptions were
  clamped to two lines and titles were cut off with "...", at any size. They now
  show up to five lines, titles wrap, and thumbnails are larger.
- The text column is capped at a readable width and the rest goes to episodes.

Hover an episode to preview it:
- Same behaviour as the rows on the home screen, using the same player.

Less clutter:
- Removed Time, Time remaining, Video, Director, Studio, Media Overview, Audio
  tracks, Subtitle tracks and Credits. The description, Genre and Studios stay.
- The rating and video-quality chips above the title are gone.

Play without configuring anything:
- Audio and subtitle selectors sit above Play Now. If a Spanish track exists it
  is selected automatically — preferring a Latin American one when the file
  labels it — and subtitles start Off. Press play and it is already right.
- Works for episodes too: a series carries no track list of its own, so each
  episode resolves its own when you click it.

Report a problem:
- A button next to Play Now opens five fixed choices: it does not play, there is
  no sound, the subtitles do not show, the video does not match the description,
  it is in another language. No typing.
- Reports go to Jellyseerr and appear in the notifications panel above the
  request history. The button only shows for titles Jellyseerr knows about.

Notes:
- Restart Jellyfin after install
- Hard refresh (Ctrl + F5) once after upgrading

v3.7.0.9 (custom fork)

Weight and language cleanup. The plugin shipped a full avatar system and nine
UI languages; this release keeps only what this server actually uses.

Avatars removed:
- The plugin embedded its own avatar system: 635 avatar images, a DiceBear
  generator with 30 styles, an avatar picker and an Avatar tab in settings.
  Jellyfin's own user image already takes priority everywhere it was used, so
  the generated avatars only ever appeared for users with no picture set.
  Everything is gone; users without a picture now get their initial in a
  circle, and any avatar plugin you install works as it should.
- Download drops from 16.8 MB to 6.1 MB and the DLL from 23 MB to 11.3 MB.

Two languages instead of nine:
- Only English and Latin American Spanish ship now. Spanish is the default and
  is the bundle loaded up front; English is fetched only if selected. The other
  seven bundles (Turkish, German, French, Russian, Italian, Japanese,
  Portuguese) are removed.
- The language selector in Settings and in the music player now offers
  Automatic / Español (Latinoamérica) / English. An existing preference for a
  removed language falls back to Spanish rather than breaking.
- 40 interface strings had no entry in any language file and were rendering
  hardcoded Turkish. Both languages are now verified key-for-key identical, so
  no untranslated text can appear.
- Content-language defaults that still pointed at Turkish (trailer lookups,
  Seerr requests, cinema pre-roll region) now default to es-MX.

Faster:
- First-load JavaScript cut from 2091 KB to 1833 KB (-12%), and 9 fewer modules
  are loaded at startup.
- The two placeholder images (default album art and the missing-actor photo)
  were stored as full-colour PNGs at 8x the weight they needed; re-encoded,
  they look identical.

Notes:
- Restart Jellyfin after install
- Hard refresh (Ctrl + F5) once after upgrading

v3.7.0.8 (custom fork)

Performance release. No feature changes — this is an audit of how the plugin
is delivered and how hard it works once loaded.

Faster loading:
- Plugin assets were served uncompressed. The plugin registers its static
  files ahead of Jellyfin's own compression, so nothing ever compressed them.
  They are now sent as Brotli or gzip, with each file encoded once and reused.
- Assets carried "max-age=0, must-revalidate", so every page load fired 80+
  conditional requests that all came back "not modified". Asset URLs are now
  pinned to the plugin version and cached for a year; installing a new version
  changes the URLs, so upgrades still take effect immediately.
- First-load JavaScript cut from 2630 KB to 2091 KB (-20%). watchlist.js and
  the Seerr item bridge (400 KB of modal and sharing UI) no longer load at
  startup, and only the language you actually use is fetched instead of both
  Turkish and English.
- index.html was also being sent uncompressed, including the ~41 KB startup
  script this plugin injects into it.

Smaller download:
- The plugin embedded 634 avatar images stored at 800x800 for pictures shown
  as small circles, plus an 813 KB catalogue icon. Re-encoded at a sensible
  size, so the DLL drops from 63 MB to 23 MB and this download from 54.8 MB
  to 16.7 MB. Avatars are unchanged at the size they are displayed.

Smoother in use:
- Four always-on DOM observers ran their work on every single page change
  rather than once per frame, including one doing four full-page searches per
  change during startup.

Fixes:
- An Arr lookup that failed or was cancelled left its cache slot occupied by
  the failed request, so every later lookup for that item failed instantly
  until Jellyfin was restarted. One user closing a tab could trigger it.
- Music player button.js pointed at two files that do not exist.
- Embedded asset lookups scanned all 855 resources on every request, and could
  match a partial filename.

Notes:
- Restart Jellyfin after install
- Hard refresh (Ctrl + F5) once after upgrading

v3.7.0.7 (custom fork)

Studio Collections now match by brand, not by a single studio entry:
- A collection used to bind to exactly one Jellyfin studio, chosen by
  whichever matching name came first alphabetically. "Marvel Studios" and
  "Marvel Entertainment" scored identically, so the Marvel card bound to
  Marvel Entertainment and showed 2 titles instead of 12.
- Jellyfin creates a separate studio entry for every distinct name in your
  metadata, so one brand spans several: Civil War is tagged Marvel Studios
  while Deadpool and Spider-Verse are tagged Marvel Entertainment. Picking
  any single entry loses titles, so collections now include all of them.
  On a 338-studio library this also merges Walt Disney Pictures (4 entries),
  DC (4), Warner Bros. (2) and DreamWorks (3).
- Matching is now driven by one shared rule set with word-boundary matching,
  so a collection can no longer pick up unrelated studios by accident.
  Accents, "&" and "+" are handled consistently.

Fixes:
- The studio list was capped at 300 entries. On larger libraries that cut off
  Walt Disney Pictures, Warner Bros. and Universal entirely; it is now fully
  paged and limited to what your user can see.
- The minimum-rating filter no longer runs on the check that decides whether
  a collection exists, so a collection whose titles all sit below the
  threshold no longer disappears from the home row.
- Clicking a collection opens a dedicated view that lists every title in the
  brand. Jellyfin's built-in studio page can only show one studio at a time.

New: Studio Collection Settings gains a read-only matching report, showing
which studio entries each collection covers, how many titles that yields, and
which studios belong to no collection.

Notes:
- Restart Jellyfin after install
- Hard refresh (Ctrl + F5) is required: cached studio data is reset by this
  version

v3.7.0.6 (custom fork)

Library Collections hero rotation:
- The rotating hero card no longer repeats a title that is already visible in
  the row below it. Each row now loads a small reserve of extra titles beyond
  the ones it displays, and the hero picks from those, so every 5-minute swap
  shows something new instead of duplicating a card on screen.
- If a library holds fewer titles than the row shows, the hero falls back to
  picking from everything available, as before.

Notes:
- Restart Jellyfin after install
- Hard refresh (Ctrl + F5) may be required

v3.7.0.5 (custom fork)

Library Collections improvements:
- Enabled by default now, together with its hero card.
- Fixed display order: Peliculas, Series, Doramas, Anime, Donghuas, Shows,
  Documentales, Collections. Collections always stays last; a newly added
  library slots in before it. Matching ignores accents, so "Peliculas" and
  "Peliculas" with the accent behave the same.
- Library Collections now sits right after Studio Collections in
  Home Section Order, unless you reordered it yourself.
- The large hero card of each category now changes to a random title every
  5 minutes. Rows are staggered so they do not all change at once, and a
  row is skipped while you hover it or while its trailer is playing.
- Trailer playback is disabled in the Collections category only: BoxSets
  carry no trailer, so it could not work there.

Fixes:
- Fixed the clipped left/right scroll arrows in the Library Collections rows.
  These rows were missing the container padding and the button styling that
  every other home row gets, so the arrows were cut off at the edge and
  rendered flat instead of as circular buttons. Card sizing and the progress
  bar in these rows now match the rest of the home screen too.
- The hero card now releases its trailer frame and backdrop image when it is
  replaced, instead of leaking one of each per swap.

Notes:
- Restart Jellyfin after install
- Hard refresh (Ctrl + F5) may be required

v3.7.0.4 (custom fork)

New: Library Collections
- Adds one home row per Jellyfin library (Anime, Documentales, Donghuas,
  Doramas, Peliculas, Series, Shows, ...), each showing its content plus a
  See All link.
- Categories are detected automatically from your libraries, so renaming or
  adding one keeps working. Utility folders (Downloads) are excluded.
- Each category has its own enable/disable checkbox under
  Studio Collection Settings > Library Collections.
- Card count per category is configurable (default 12).
- Disabled by default on fresh installs.

Fixes:
- update_meta.sh now emits a valid ISO timestamp on macOS/BSD
  (%7N is a GNU date extension and was written out literally).

Notes:
- Restart Jellyfin after install
- Hard refresh (Ctrl + F5) may be required
